text:
Inside a building at eight hundred megahertz, the I T U indoor model predicts about seventy-nine decibels of loss across thirty meters of open office, and about eighty-eight with a floor between.
Each wall adds its own loss: drywall about two decibels, concrete block ten, poured concrete fourteen, and low-E glass about twenty.
That is why an emergency radio system needs antennas on every floor.

Now a blurry phone photo of the same plan.
It grades an F: the resolution is too low, it is rotated, it was taken at an angle, and it has no scale.
The app lists each problem with its fix, and asks for a better file.
Drop the new file right in the box.

Say yes to add the plan to the project.
Then the [2D](/tˌu dˈi/) and [3D](/θɹˌi dˈi/) Models, Auto-Design, the device layouts, the cable lengths and the Materials list all use it.
Tick boxes turn each layer on and off: walls, doors, windows, room tags, and each system's devices and cabling.

Part six covers R F engineering: decibels, transmission lines and V S W R, antennas, propagation and [Fresnel](/fɹənˈɛl/) zones, path loss models, fading, noise, modulation and interference.
Part seven covers design concepts, from surge protection and P o E to Wi-Fi, [DAS](/dˈæs/), structured cabling and drawing scales.
Every section ends with industry best practices.

Markers, max hold, the waterfall and the measurements work like a bench analyzer: channel power, occupied bandwidth, adjacent channel power, noise floor and limit lines.
Guided tests set it up for you: [BDA](/bˌidˌiˈA/) uplink noise and oscillation, the donor signal for each channel, and the downlink check.
Add to [Live](/lˈIv/) Signal Readings sends the readings to the [ERCES](/ˈɜɹsiz/) grid test.

Benchmarks grade the receiver against a signal generator.
Use only measurement-grade equipment for acceptance tests.
The certification tests cover the [ERCES](/ˈɜɹsiz/) grid test, the F C C emission mask and booster checks, and each one saves a signed report for Reports.

Space weather comes live from NOAA's Space Weather Prediction Center: the K P index, the storm level, and the chance of radio blackouts.
Each download is checked, and marked Verified, with the time.
During a geomagnetic storm, a warning shows beside compass bearings on other pages, so you aim with G P S instead.
Offline, it shows the last forecast and when it was downloaded.

Weather and Radar shows the latest report from the nearest National Weather Service station: temperature, feels-like, wind and gusts, humidity, pressure and visibility.
Each download is checked, and marked Verified, with the time.
With no internet, it shows the last weather downloaded, and how long ago.

NOAA maps adds the satellite view, lightning from the last five minutes, severe storm outlooks, alerts and forecast maps.
Each one shows its time, and the last copy is kept for offline use.
